text:
Elaine: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a 'tile + bridge' refactor to incrementally carve small, testable tiles and introduce a thin bridge layer as a temporary adaptor. Goal: reduce coupling, speed owner handoffs, and pay down debt without a big-bang cutover. Asking for tradeoffs, obvious risks, and rollout constraints.

Tom: sounds promising. my main worry is extra runtime hop/cost from the bridge. need latency/cost estimates before we commit.

Raj: we can measure with a synthetic harness. rough guess: bridge adds 3–12ms depending on payload but simplifies ownership which reduces coordination overhead. worth quantifying.

Kevin: KV cache consistency is the other risk. bridge must not become a secondary source of truth. prefer bridge stateless + do not own cache.

Sophia: agree — bridge should be stateless and strictly a translation/dispatch layer. recommend protobuf v2 contracts and schema validation on ingress. also think about observability hooks.

Elaine: rollout sketch: 1) extract single tile (enricher) behind feature flag; 2) deploy bridge shim that routes flagged traffic to tile; 3) canary 1% -> 5% -> 25%; 4) increase traffic and flip default; 5) remove legacy path when tile coverage >= 95% and tests green. pre-reqs: integration tests, load harness, quality diffs.

Tom: can we add an automatic safety guard: abort if p95 latency increases > 10% or error rate > 0.2% during canary?

Raj: +1. also tie bridge to a short TTL tech-debt ticket (auto-remind in 90 days). don't let it become permanent.

Kevin: tracing: mark a 'bridge-hop' span and tag tenant/route. that'll make perf deltas obvious in traces. use existing sampling.

Sophia: quality monitoring note — run output-diffing on prompt/response for any LLM calls proxied by the bridge. register baseline prompts and watch for regressions.

Elaine: sample config for feature-flagged routing (will add to RFC PR):
```json
{
  "route": "/api/enrich",
  "treatment": "bridge-v1",
  "percent": 1
}
```

Raj: perf budget should be part of the RFC. if p95 delta crosses threshold, rollback. record exact rollback procedure in runbook.

Tom: noticed some header-null errors in early dogfood canary yesterday — I pushed a fix to bridge shim to default missing headers. small patch ready.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary started for bridge-v1 -> 1% traffic (env: staging).

Elaine: thanks. action items: I will open RFC follow-up PR with rollout phases, test checklist, perf budgets, and a tech-debt ticket to delete the bridge after cutover. link will be in the PR. tagging @Tom @Raj @Sophia to review the contract + runbook.

Raj: suggest adding a small KPI: 'bridge deletion target date' and estimated points so PMs can prioritize.

Kevin: plus add an observability dashboard tile for the bridge: p50/p95/p99, error rate, and a traffic split gauge.

Sophia: and a quality baseline dashboard for prompt diff false positives.

Elaine: agreed on all. I'll draft the PR tonight. :shipit:
